message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that’s usually scheduled as part of its routine maintenance program. In practice:

| Step | Typical Duration |
|------|------------------|
| **Preparation & cleaning** (remove old paint, sandblast, wash) | ~1–2 weeks |
| **Priming** (apply protective primer coat) | ~1 week |
| **Painting** (apply new paint layers – usually two coats) | ~1–2 weeks |
| **Inspection & touch‑ups** | ~1 week |

So the whole operation normally takes **about 4–6 weeks** (roughly 1–1½ months).  

This schedule aligns with the tower’s official repaint cycle: the structure is repainted every **seven years**, and each repaint typically requires around **two months** of work. The exact timing can vary depending on weather conditions, the extent of surface preparation needed, and whether additional structural repairs are performed concurrently.
